title: T1078.001 — Valid Accounts - Default Accounts
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Valid Accounts - Default Accounts with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Animated diagram with six nodes: an attacker VPS, an internet scan grid, a small-office router, an IP camera with a default admin login, a botnet controller, and a SOC network monitor. The animation shows the attacker scanning the internet, logging into the camera with the default account, installing bot malware, the camera joining a botnet, the SOC spotting the traffic, and the device being hardened.

steps.title: Scanning
steps.caption: A rented server drives a scan grid that knocks on Telnet port 23 and on well-known admin URLs across huge IP ranges. It is looking for any device that answers with a login form. This is the same behavior the Mirai family made famous, and it never stopped
steps.defender: IdP and SaaS audit logs record token issuance, consent, sign-in location and API access.

steps.title: Attack traffic
steps.caption: Weeks later the botnet is ordered to attack. The camera sends crafted DNS queries to open resolvers, which send large replies to the victim, hiding the true source. On the office link this shows up as a strong outbound traffic spike at 3 a.m., when nobody is working
steps.defender: IdP and SaaS audit logs record token issuance, consent, sign-in location and API access.

steps.title: SOC notice
steps.caption: A network monitor flags traffic from the office to a known-bad controller address. The analyst pulls device and firewall logs, finds the NetFlow spike, and traces back to the syslog line: a remote admin login on the camera with the default account. Three evidence chips now line up: the login, the spike, and the controller IP

steps.title: Fix
steps.caption: The office owner updates the firmware, replaces the default password with a unique one, disables Telnet, and moves the camera to an isolated IoT VLAN. The device can still do its job, but it can no longer be a door into the office or a hidden attacker on the internet
steps.defender: IdP and SaaS audit logs record token issuance, consent, sign-in location and API access.
